goal: Stop the node from recording a block as flushed when the underlying block or undo file write actually failed.
Prevents block-index metadata and chainstate from getting ahead of data that may not be durable on disk.
reviewability: Ready: discussion is settled, remaining comments are style nits.
agreement: Strong support from three reviewers who examined durability implications in depth (arejula27, mzumsande, optout21).

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because it closes a data-integrity gap where block-index metadata could be written and m_last_flushed_block advanced despite an unflushed block or undo file, risking BLOCK_HAVE_DATA pointing at missing data (mzumsande's blocksdir scenario).
Resolves a TODO left open since #27866 and complements #34897's m_last_flushed_block invariant, but the failure mode it fixes (permanent fsync failure) is rare.

result.summary: This PR changes FlushStateToDisk() so that when FlushChainstateBlockFile() fails, the function returns the error immediately instead of proceeding to write block-index metadata and coins data and advancing m_last_flushed_block. It adds a regression test that injects a block-file flush failure and checks that the flush return value, error state, and m_last_flushed_block all reflect the failure. The change resolves a TODO left in the code since PR #27866, building on the m_last_flushed_block invariant introduced in #34897.
result.problem: Previously, a failed block or undo file flush requested shutdown but still let FlushStateToDisk() write chainstate/block-index metadata and advance the last-flushed-block marker, so the on-disk metadata could claim a block's data is present and durable when it is not. This risks metadata/data mismatch (e.g., BLOCK_HAVE_DATA set while the actual block file write failed), especially relevant when blocksdir is stored separately from the rest of the data directory, as mzumsande noted.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Labeled Validation; changes FlushStateToDisk()'s handling of a flush failure, directly affecting chainstate integrity and the m_last_flushed_block invariant introduced in #34897.
categories.rationale: Closes a data-integrity gap where metadata could be persisted ahead of actual block/undo durability, a scenario mzumsande identified as potentially causing real corruption when -blocksdir is separate and its fsync fails permanently. It resolves a TODO deliberately left open since #27866 pending a caller audit and test, which this PR now provides, but the triggering condition (permanent I/O failure) is rare, keeping it below P1.

uncertainties: Whether the underlying failure scenario (permanent fsync failure with separate blocksdir) has ever been observed in practice, or is purely theoretical, affects how high P2 vs P1 should be.
The open follow-up PR #35731 proposes further hardening; unclear whether reviewers consider this PR sufficient on its own or a stepping stone.
result.card: This PR changes Chainstate::FlushStateToDisk() to return the flush error immediately when FlushChainstateBlockFile() fails, instead of continuing to write block-index metadata and coins data and advancing m_last_flushed_block past an unflushed block. It closes a data-integrity gap identified back in PR #27866 (left as a TODO) and reinforces the m_last_flushed_block invariant added in #34897. Reviewer mzumsande's analysis identified a concrete corruption risk when -blocksdir is stored separately and its fsync fails permanently, after which BLOCK_HAVE_DATA could be set while block data is actually missing. Three reviewers (arejula27, mzumsande, optout21) gave ACK or Concept ACK after detailed local testing, and all raised concerns (LogWarning duplication, m_next_write timing, test noise) were resolved by the author with explanations or fixes. The PR is small, self-contained, and appears ready to merge; a related follow-up (#35731) proposes further hardening of the same invariant.
